Payment does not define all participants.
The vendor is not the only recipient.
The statute requires advance notice.

questions.stem: A remote officer identifies a longtime acquaintance by personal knowledge. What explanation belongs on the recording?
options: Only the person's payment method
Only the vendor's approval
No explanation because familiarity is enough
How the officer knows the person and how long
questions.explanation: The recording must explain the personal-knowledge relationship and duration.
feedback: Payment is not the required explanation.
Vendor approval does not establish personal knowledge.
The statute expressly requires the explanation.
Correct. The recording must explain the personal-knowledge relationship and duration.

questions.stem: A credible witness identifies the remote principal. What relationship explanation must the recording include from the witness?
options: Only the notary's course grade
Only the vendor's annual subscription
How and how long the witness knows the principal
Only the witness's invoice number
questions.explanation: The recording includes the witness's relationship and duration explanation.
feedback: The notary's grade does not explain the witness's knowledge.
Subscription history is unrelated.
Correct. The recording includes the witness's relationship and duration explanation.
An invoice does not supply personal knowledge.

questions.stem: An electronic certificate is complete. What integrity step follows attaching the signature, seal and wording?
options: Remove the audio-video notation
Render the document tamper-evident
Convert it into an untracked editable image only
Delete the certificate
questions.explanation: The electronic document must reveal subsequent changes.
feedback: The remote notation remains required where applicable.
Correct. The electronic document must reveal subsequent changes.
An untracked image alone does not establish tamper evidence.
The certificate remains required.

questions.stem: A journal designer wants to collect electronic signatures of principals and witnesses in Nevada's statutory electronic journal. What does the section state?
options: The electronic journal does not include those electronic signatures
Every signature must be stored there
Only signatures may replace every other entry field
The principal decides whether the law applies
questions.explanation: The statute expressly excludes those electronic signatures from this journal.
feedback: Correct. The statute expressly excludes those electronic signatures from this journal.
The section states the opposite journal rule.
The other required information remains.
The statute governs the journal content.

questions.stem: A state employee performs an electronic notarial act within government employment scope. May the officer charge a notarial fee?
options: Yes, every employee may always charge $25
Yes, if a manager asks
Yes, if performed on a laptop
No, the government-scope electronic fee restriction applies
questions.explanation: State and local government employees may not charge for electronic acts within that scope.
feedback: The exception overrides the general electronic fee schedule.
A manager cannot waive it.
The device does not change employment scope.
Correct. State and local government employees may not charge for electronic acts within that scope.

questions.stem: An electronic-signature device becomes insecure. What must precede resuming electronic acts?
options: Only tell a customer
Only make the password shorter
Acquire new technology and send SOS the specified electronic notice with the new signature
Only restart the browser
questions.explanation: The section requires cessation until replacement and the specified SOS notice.
feedback: Customer notice does not satisfy state notice.
A weaker password does not cure the device.
Correct. The section requires cessation until replacement and the specified SOS notice.
Restarting does not establish a secure replacement.

questions.stem: A former registrant renews within three months using the same signature, with no prior revocation or denial. What does the limited exception address?
options: A transfer of registration to the vendor
The duty to render signature technology ineffective
Authority to act during an expired gap
A waiver of seven-year record retention
questions.explanation: The exception concerns destruction or disabling of the signature technology under its conditions.
feedback: Registration remains personal.
Correct. The exception concerns destruction or disabling of the signature technology under its conditions.
It does not grant interim authority.
Retention is a separate duty.

cards.title: Instruction minimum
cards.front: What is the ordinary mandatory course's statutory minimum?
cards.rule: At least three hours of instruction and an examination.
cards.boundary: The course may be provided by SOS or an approved vendor.
cards.mixup: Instructional hours do not establish examination duration.

cards.title: Renewers study too
cards.front: Which ordinary applicants take the mandatory course?
cards.rule: First applicants and renewing appointees are expressly included.
cards.boundary: SOS may also direct specified violators or suspended appointees to study.
cards.mixup: Experience does not remove the renewal training requirement.

cards.title: Separate course and test
cards.front: How is the traditional LMS route completed?
cards.rule: Enroll in and complete both the Commission Course and Commission Exam separately.
cards.boundary: Finishing a video alone does not complete the examination.
cards.mixup: An automatically displayed course badge may not establish the separate exam result.

cards.title: Payment location
cards.front: Where does the current LMS send official payments?
cards.rule: SilverFlume during application submission.
cards.boundary: The LMS separately lists traditional and electronic training at $45 each.
cards.mixup: A training payment is separate from the statutory application fee.

cards.title: Progress preservation
cards.front: What actions help preserve course completion evidence?
cards.rule: Close the player at completion and save the specified screenshot or PDF proof.
cards.boundary: Desktop use is recommended to reduce mobile connectivity-related progress loss.
cards.mixup: An open player is not necessarily saved completion progress.

cards.title: Bond and oath
cards.front: What goes to the proper county clerk?
cards.rule: The $10,000 bond together with the oath for filing and recording.
cards.boundary: The clerk supplies the prescribed certification to SOS.
cards.mixup: A purchase receipt is different from a recorded bond and oath.

cards.title: Nonresident filing county
cards.front: Where does an adjoining-state applicant file the bond?
cards.rule: The Nevada county in which the qualifying business or employment is located.
cards.boundary: A resident applicant follows the residence-county route.
cards.mixup: A client's property county does not determine this applicant filing.

cards.title: Assurance purpose
cards.front: What is the bond conditioned to protect?
cards.rule: Indemnification for damage from the specified unlawful notarial conduct, payable to the State of Nevada.
cards.boundary: Aggregate surety liability does not exceed the penal sum.
cards.mixup: The bond does not guarantee the customer's business success.

cards.title: License evidence
cards.front: What extra evidence accompanies a bordering resident's application?
cards.rule: The specified address affidavit and state/local business-license evidence, with the employer affidavit when applicable.
cards.boundary: Self-employed and employed applicants have distinct supporting evidence.
cards.mixup: A private recommendation does not replace business licensing.

cards.title: Matching name forms
cards.front: What consistency governs application and bond names?
cards.rule: Use the same permitted form of the applicant's name.
cards.boundary: The official signature remains consistent with the original application signature.
cards.mixup: A familiar given-name form can be permitted while inconsistent forms remain a problem.

cards.title: Term and certificate
cards.front: What two timing facts must be kept separate?
cards.rule: The term starts on the bond effective date, and acts require an issued appointment certificate.
cards.boundary: A later certificate does not restart the statutory commencement.
cards.mixup: An effective bond by itself is insufficient authority.

cards.title: Territorial scope
cards.front: Where do traditional appointment powers operate?
cards.rule: Anywhere within Nevada for four years unless sooner removed.
cards.boundary: The appointment and electronic registration do not confer another state's powers.
cards.mixup: Adjoining-state residence eligibility does not authorize acts there.

cards.title: Assurance continuity
cards.front: What happens when required coverage ends or its penal sum is exhausted?
cards.rule: The appointment is suspended by operation of law.
cards.boundary: The section supplies a conditional replacement-bond reinstatement process before term end.
cards.mixup: A printed unexpired certificate does not cure missing coverage.

cards.title: Amended details
cards.front: What follows an amended appointment certificate?
cards.rule: Destroy the old stamp, obtain the matching new stamp and notify the surety.
cards.boundary: Specified changes require the timely amendment and fee.
cards.mixup: An amended public record should not be paired with obsolete stamp details.

cards.title: Required stamp
cards.front: What authenticating features must the ordinary stamp have?
cards.rule: Indelible reproducible ink, prescribed appointment data, a legible rectangular imprint within the statutory size.
cards.boundary: The Great Seal is optional, and nonresident status adds the specified word.
cards.mixup: An embosser does not replace the required stamped statement.

cards.title: Extended relatives
cards.front: How broad is Nevada's family restriction?
cards.rule: It includes specified relatives by marriage or blood and relatives of the domestic partner.
cards.boundary: The listed definition includes step, half, adopted and certain sibling-child connections.
cards.mixup: A transaction unrelated to family finances does not erase the relationship.

cards.title: Domestic partners
cards.front: What direct restriction covers a domestic partner?
cards.rule: The notary may not perform the stated signature-related act for that partner.
cards.boundary: The rule is separate from financial benefit.
cards.mixup: A fee waiver does not remove partner status.

cards.title: Limited fee exceptions
cards.front: Which compensation exceptions need precise treatment?
cards.rule: Nevada-licensed attorney legal fees and registered document-preparation service fees have specified exceptions.
cards.boundary: These address the compensation ground.
cards.mixup: They do not erase independent relationship or named-instrument prohibitions.

cards.title: Employer ownership claim
cards.front: Who owns the stamp, journal and appointment certificate?
cards.rule: They are the notary's personal property and may not be withheld.
cards.boundary: The rule applies even when someone else funded the items.
cards.mixup: Employer payment does not confer the right to retain them.

cards.title: Advertising limits
cards.front: What does a non-English notary advertisement require?
cards.rule: The prescribed same-language notice, conspicuous when written, under the statutory conditions.
cards.boundary: Specified non-English titles are independently prohibited for nonattorneys.
cards.mixup: A disclaimer does not authorize a prohibited title.

cards.title: Ordinary appearance
cards.front: What does an ordinary acknowledgment require from the signer?
cards.rule: The signer presents the instrument in person and the officer establishes identity.
cards.boundary: Electronic remote appearance requires its separate legal route.
cards.mixup: A courier's delivery does not equal the principal's appearance.

cards.title: Identity evidence
cards.front: What documentary alternatives does Nevada expressly identify?
cards.rule: The listed photo-and-signature document, consular-card route and conditional senior/prisoner routes.
cards.boundary: Apply each route's actual conditions.
cards.mixup: Do not import another state's expiration or document-feature rule without Nevada support.

cards.title: Jurat components
cards.front: What does a jurat certify?
cards.rule: Signing in the officer's presence and swearing or affirming the document's truth.
cards.boundary: The officer also establishes the affiant's identity.
cards.mixup: A recognized old signature does not replace present jurat execution.

cards.title: Directed signing
cards.front: Who can sign for a physically unable principal?
cards.rule: A directed person other than the notarial officer, with the required explanatory notation.
cards.boundary: The rule requires principal and helper to appear when signing occurs.
cards.mixup: The officer cannot assume the helper role under this Nevada procedure.

cards.title: Remote geography
cards.front: Where must the electronic officer be during a remote act?
cards.rule: The electronic notary must be physically in Nevada while performing the remote act.
cards.boundary: An overseas principal has additional known-prohibition and United States-connection conditions.
cards.mixup: A Nevada mailing address does not establish the officer's physical location.

cards.title: Contemporaneous entry
cards.front: When is the ordinary act entered?
cards.rule: When the act is performed.
cards.boundary: A narrowly defined combined-entry option exists.
cards.mixup: A weekend reconstruction from memory is different from the required timing.

cards.title: Combined entry
cards.front: When may more than one act share an entry?
cards.rule: Same person, same time, on one document or similar documents.
cards.boundary: The entry still documents the covered acts.
cards.mixup: A single end-of-day entry for unrelated clients does not fit.

cards.title: Signature exception
cards.front: What conditions accompany the employer/coworker journal-signature exception?
cards.rule: Prior act within six months, personal knowledge and the specified ordinary-course business relationship.
cards.boundary: The resulting evidence description is known personally.
cards.mixup: Familiarity alone does not satisfy all conditions.

cards.title: Travel evidence
cards.front: What additional journal entry follows a charged trip?
cards.rule: The fee amount and dates and times travel began and ended.
cards.boundary: Travel charges have advance-agreement and rate-cap conditions.
cards.mixup: Recording only the acknowledgment price omits the separate travel evidence.

cards.title: Hourly bands
cards.front: What are the ordinary travel-rate ceilings?
cards.rule: $15 per hour for requested travel between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m., and $30 between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m.
cards.boundary: A two-hour minimum is allowed, followed by pro rata charging.
cards.mixup: The schedule is an hourly travel rule, separate from act fees.

cards.title: Ordinary retention trigger
cards.front: What starts the ordinary journal's post-service period?
cards.rule: The person ceasing to be a notary, followed by seven years.
cards.boundary: Old entries do not expire merely because each is seven years old.
cards.mixup: The last entry and cessation can occur on different dates.

cards.title: Incomplete remote act
cards.front: Does an unsuccessful remote session erase the recording duty?
cards.rule: No. Keep the recording at least seven years regardless of completion.
cards.boundary: The principal's refund does not change that record duty.
cards.mixup: An aborted act and an absent recording are different facts.

cards.title: Separate protected records
cards.front: What belongs outside the electronic journal itself?
cards.rule: The required audiovisual recording and nonrequired personally identifying information.
cards.boundary: The journal has its own required transaction fields.
cards.mixup: Separating records does not permit deleting the recording.

cards.title: Backup protection
cards.front: Who backs up the electronic journal under the rule?
cards.rule: The officer and the solution provider securely back it up.
cards.boundary: Journal entries cannot be deleted or have content or sequence changed after entry.
cards.mixup: A live editable spreadsheet alone does not supply the required record integrity.

cards.title: Authorized recording access
cards.front: How are recording recipients determined?
cards.rule: Use the specified principal, official, court-process and party-authorized categories.
cards.boundary: Ordinary journal public inspection is a separate rule.
cards.mixup: Public journal access does not automatically make every recording public.

cards.title: Registration foundation
cards.front: What comes before electronic registration?
cards.rule: A compliant traditional appointment and the required separate electronic study and examination.
cards.boundary: The LMS expressly puts the traditional commission first.
cards.mixup: A webcam purchase does not supply the underlying commission.

cards.title: Effective registration
cards.front: What makes electronic registration effective under the rule?
cards.rule: The SOS processing system update indicating registration.
cards.boundary: The ordinary certificate and provider account serve other roles.
cards.mixup: An attempted payment does not alone establish the official update.

cards.title: Broken session
cards.front: What follows a broken link or participant exit?
cards.rule: Restart performance from the beginning, including identity confirmation.
cards.boundary: The specified compromised-quality situation also triggers restart.
cards.mixup: Reopening the same file does not waive renewed performance.

cards.title: Electronic integrity
cards.front: What completes the electronic record's authentication?
cards.rule: Attach or logically associate signature, seal and certificate, then render the document tamper-evident.
cards.boundary: Include the audio-video notation when applicable.
cards.mixup: A decorative seal picture does not establish the whole process.

cards.title: Invalid device
cards.front: What follows learning signature technology is ineffective or insecure?
cards.rule: Cease electronic acts until replacement technology is acquired and the specified SOS notice is sent.
cards.boundary: Keep the technology current and unrevoked through reasonable steps.
cards.mixup: An active subscription does not cure a compromised device.

cards.title: Ninety-day certificate
cards.front: How long is the required course certificate valid?
cards.rule: Ninety days from issuance.
cards.boundary: The regulation also requires the stated SOS validation stamp.
cards.mixup: Course access duration and certificate validity are separate.

cards.title: LMS completion window
cards.front: Which three activities does the official LMS include in its ninety-day instruction?
cards.rule: Training, examinations and payment.
cards.boundary: Payment is made through SilverFlume as directed.
cards.mixup: Watching the course alone does not complete all three.

cards.title: Official evidence
cards.front: What proof should accompany the portal application?
cards.rule: The saved official Exam Completion notification or certificate, with supporting documents and payment.
cards.boundary: A screenshot or PDF is expressly suggested by the LMS.
cards.mixup: A commercial practice badge is not official exam completion.

cards.title: Unverified test metrics
cards.front: What ordinary examination metrics remain unconfirmed in the opened sources?
cards.rule: Question count, duration and numerical passing threshold.
cards.boundary: The principal's remote KBA has separately stated metrics.
cards.mixup: KBA's eighty percent is not proof of a Commission Exam passing score.

cards.title: Provider authority
cards.front: What makes a third-party course eligible for the statutory route?
cards.rule: SOS authorization of a qualified provider subject to its terms.
cards.boundary: The source permits approved third-party provision.
cards.mixup: Self-issued marketing claims do not establish official approval.

cards.title: Known falsehood
cards.front: What must an officer avoid certifying?
cards.rule: An instrument containing a statement the officer knows is false.
cards.boundary: A paid request does not change the prohibition.
cards.mixup: A truthful journal cannot cure a knowingly false certificate.

cards.title: Complete record
cards.front: How are ordinary unused information spaces resolved?
cards.rule: The signer fills them, designates not applicable or lines them through under the rule.
cards.boundary: A limited additional-signer-line rule applies when the current notarization clearly excludes it.
cards.mixup: An unused additional signature line differs from an unresolved information blank.

cards.title: Restricted copies
cards.front: Which photocopies are expressly prohibited?
cards.rule: Birth, death and marriage certificates and divorce decrees.
cards.boundary: General private-document copy powers do not override these exclusions.
cards.mixup: A perfect image does not remove the document-category restriction.

cards.title: Voluntary execution
cards.front: When may competence or voluntariness support refusal?
cards.rule: When the officer is unsatisfied about competence, capacity or knowing and voluntary signing.
cards.boundary: The section also preserves other refusal authority subject to law.
cards.mixup: Customer urgency does not establish voluntary understanding.

cards.title: No bare stamp
cards.front: What must accompany use of the notarial stamp?
cards.rule: A document containing a notarial certificate for the act.
cards.boundary: A document containing only a signature is separately prohibited.
cards.mixup: A customer asking for just a stamp does not remove certification duties.

training-process.summary: Complete Nevada's required traditional education and separate official examination before seeking appointment.

sections.heading: The required course
sections.body: NRS 240.018 requires at least three instructional hours plus an examination. It includes initial applicants, renewing appointees and specified enforcement cases directed to study by SOS. Courses may be offered by SOS or an approved vendor. The current official LMS requires separate enrollment and completion of the Commission Course and Commission Exam. A private study product's badge does not establish completion of that official route.

sections.heading: LMS and application evidence
sections.body: The LMS directs payment through SilverFlume during application submission and separately lists traditional and electronic training fees. It recommends desktop study and closing the completed training player to save progress. Save a screenshot or PDF of completion evidence and attach the specified Exam Completion notification or certificate with the application documents and payment. Those administrative actions support proof of prerequisites while the state appointment remains a separate decision.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A first applicant completes the traditional course, enrolls separately in the Commission Exam and saves the actual completion evidence. The applicant then prepares the county bond-and-oath evidence and SilverFlume packet. A completed video alone does not establish the separate examination or issued appointment.

keyFacts: At least three instructional hours plus an examination are required.
Renewing traditional appointees also complete mandatory study.
The official LMS separates course and exam enrollments.
Official payment occurs through SilverFlume.

county-filing.summary: Keep Nevada's county recording evidence distinct from the state application and appointment.

sections.heading: Bond and oath route
sections.body: NRS 240.030 requires a ten-thousand-dollar bond and the prescribed oath. Residents file and record them with the residence county clerk. An adjoining-state applicant uses the Nevada county of the qualifying business or employment. The clerk certifies filing and recording to SOS on the prescribed form. NRS 240.033 describes the State of Nevada as obligee and sets the indemnification purpose, coverage and replacement provisions.

sections.heading: Supporting information
sections.body: The state application includes the statutory fee and satisfactory course proof. Adjoining-state applicants add address affidavits, applicable state and local licensing evidence and the employer affidavit when not self-employed. NAC 240.210 requires consistent permitted name forms on the application and bond. The statute protects residential address and telephone information on application documents that become public. Check the actual document requirements without assuming a generic vendor form satisfies each step.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A California resident works regularly at a registered Washoe County employer. The applicant assembles the required nonresident affidavit and employer licensing evidence, files the bond and oath with the Washoe clerk and uses the county certification in the state application. A California filing would not satisfy the specified Nevada county route.

keyFacts: The ordinary bond is $10,000.
The bond and oath are recorded together.
The appropriate Nevada clerk provides the required filing certification.
Adjoining-state applicants have additional affidavits and licensing evidence.

start-of-authority.summary: Appointment timing, assurance continuity and compliant supplies all affect Nevada authority to act.

sections.heading: Authority and continuing qualifications
sections.body: The statutory term runs four years unless sooner removed and commences on the bond effective date. NRS 240.030 nevertheless forbids acts before the appointment certificate has been issued. Qualification includes age eighteen, civil rights and the required residence or adjoining-state connection. NRS 240.033 suspends appointment by operation of law when required coverage ends or its penal sum is exhausted. An old printed certificate does not override that event.

sections.heading: Stamp and changed details
sections.body: NRS 240.040 requires the prescribed indelible reproducible stamped statement, readable rectangular imprint and appointment data. Nonresident stamps carry that word. Store the device securely and keep it off printed material. The amendment, loss and damage provisions have different notice periods. After an amended certificate, destroy the old stamp, obtain the matching replacement and notify the surety. A supplier must see the specified appointment-certificate evidence before manufacturing a device.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A bond becomes effective before the state finishes issuing an applicant's certificate. The term's commencement does not supply immediate acting authority. The applicant waits for issuance, then obtains a stamp using the certificate details and serves only while the appointment and required assurance remain effective.

keyFacts: Bond effectiveness and certificate issuance are separate facts.
Nevada authority operates within Nevada.
Required assurance must continue.
The stamp must match appointment information and remain secure.

family.summary: Evaluate extended family, direct benefits and professional exceptions independently.

sections.heading: Relationships and interests
sections.body: NRS 240.065 addresses instruments the officer executed or is named in, direct transaction benefits beyond the authorized fee, domestic partners and covered relatives. Its definition includes step, half and adopted relationships and specified relatives of a spouse or domestic partner. The licensed-attorney and registered-document-preparer provisions address particular compensation grounds. They do not erase independent relationship or participation restrictions.

sections.heading: Employer and advertising duties
sections.body: NRS 240.143 makes the stamp, journal and appointment certificate the notary's personal property even if another person paid. Employers may not withhold them. NRS 240.085 imposes same-language professional-limit notices under its terms and independently forbids specified non-English titles for nonattorneys. The employer has related compliance duties. Using a public appointment to endorse a product is separately prohibited by NRS 240.075.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A registered document preparer plans an ordinary paid act for a domestic partner. The preparation-fee exception addresses compensation, while the partner prohibition independently prevents that assignment. Another eligible officer must evaluate the service without treating the preparer's registration as a family-rule waiver.

keyFacts: Domestic partners are expressly covered.
Extended relative categories include adopted and step relationships.
Compensation exceptions have a limited scope.
Employer payment does not transfer ownership of notarial property.

physical-appearance.summary: Apply the evidence and appearance requirements of the particular Nevada act and service method.

sections.heading: Ordinary identity and execution
sections.body: NRS 240.1655 requires personal presentation for an ordinary acknowledgment and specifies identity routes including personal knowledge, sworn credible witnesses and listed documentary alternatives. Conditional senior and state-prisoner routes have their own predicates. A jurat includes identity, present signing and an oath or affirmation. Copy certification requires the entire presented document, subject to express document restrictions elsewhere in the chapter.

sections.heading: Accommodation and remote work
sections.body: A physically unable principal may direct someone other than the officer to sign, with the required explanatory notation. NAC 240.340 requires both principal and helper to appear at signing. Registered remote work uses separate audiovisual presence and identity rules. The officer remains physically in Nevada. An overseas principal must satisfy the known-prohibition condition and confirm the specified United States connection. Remote documentary identification combines credential presentation, analysis and the prescribed authentication or authorized proofing process.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: At a care facility, a physically unable person directs a helper to sign while both appear before the notary. The officer remains the certifying officer and adds the required directed-signature explanation. The helper's presence alone would not satisfy the regulation, and the notary cannot become the directed helper under this procedure.

keyFacts: Ordinary acknowledgment requires the signer's personal presentation.
A jurat includes present signing and an oath or affirmation.
A directed helper must be someone other than the notarial officer.
The remote officer must be physically in Nevada.

entry-timing.summary: Make contemporaneous Nevada entries with the correct transaction detail and any authorized fee evidence.

sections.heading: Journal detail and exceptions
sections.body: NRS 240.120 requires entries when acts occur, including fee, document title, date, principal name and ordinarily signature, identity evidence, oath indication and certificate type. One entry may document specified acts for the same person at the same time on one or similar documents. The journal-signature exception requires all the recent-service, personal-knowledge and employer/coworker business conditions. Credible witnesses sign in the evidence space and receive the required notation.

sections.heading: Fees and travel
sections.body: NRS 240.100 distinguishes act-fee categories and additional travel conditions. Requested travel, disclosure and advance agreement on the hourly rate are required, with separate daytime and nighttime ceilings. A two-hour minimum is permitted, followed by pro rata charging. Record the travel fee amount and travel start/end dates and times. NRS 240.110 requires a conspicuous fee table in the specified type size before fees may be charged.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A notary travels at a customer's request under a compliant advance agreement, then performs several acts for that person together on similar records. The officer evaluates the combined-entry rule and still records the actual transaction details, act fees and required travel interval evidence. One total payment amount does not by itself explain those separate services.

keyFacts: Journal entries are made when acts are performed.
Combined entries have specified person, time and document conditions.
The coworker signature exception has multiple cumulative conditions.
Travel charges require additional journal information.

retention.summary: Nevada uses distinct custody, access and retention provisions for ordinary journals, electronic journals and recordings.

sections.heading: Ordinary records
sections.body: NRS 240.120 requires a bound ordinary journal with preprinted page numbers, secure non-entry storage, public inspection and certified entry copies on request and payment. Each journal remains until seven years after the person ceases to be a notary. Lost or stolen journals are reported to SOS and appropriate law enforcement. Personal ownership of a journal does not eliminate its legal public-inspection obligation.

sections.heading: Electronic journals and recordings
sections.body: NRS 240.201 preserves the officer's sole-control duty despite employer records and requires copy capability and timely production to SOS. NAC 240.708 prevents post-entry deletion or changes to content or sequence and requires secure backup. NAC 240.710 excludes nonrequired personal identifying information and the recording itself from the journal. Recordings remain at least seven years even after incomplete remote acts, and their authorized recipients are governed separately from ordinary public journal access.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A remote session fails before completion. The officer preserves the recording for the required period while maintaining the separate electronic journal. The platform keeps the recording out of the journal itself, protects both stores and backups, and applies the recording-access categories before releasing a copy.

keyFacts: Ordinary journal retention is measured from cessation as a notary.
An incomplete remote act still has recording-retention duties.
The electronic journal and audiovisual recording remain distinct.
Employer recordkeeping does not replace the officer's obligations.

electronic-sequence.summary: Register Nevada electronic authority and configure the actual session process before offering remote services.

sections.heading: Registration and continuity
sections.body: The LMS puts a traditional commission first, then separate eRegistration course and examination. NRS 240.192 requires the additional registration, fee, proof and intended signature technology. NAC 240.658 makes effectiveness depend on the official system update. Electronic registration is coterminous with ordinary appointment and suspended when the underlying appointment no longer exists. Specified electronic changes have a ten-day notice and fee requirement.

sections.heading: Session integrity
sections.body: The parties agree to the audiovisual method. The officer identifies the actual signed electronic document, informs all participants about recording and records required personal-knowledge or credible-witness explanations. NAC 240.680 requires a restart, including identity confirmation, after participant exit, a broken link or the specified quality compromise. Complete the signature, seal and certificate association and tamper-evidence step. Insecure signature technology requires cessation until replacement and the prescribed SOS notice.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A remote principal exits while locating a missing attachment and returns shortly afterward. The officer restarts performance under the rule and reconfirms identity, then identifies the actual signed record. Keeping the same browser tab and file title does not remove the restart requirement.

keyFacts: Electronic authority requires separate state registration.
Electronic registration follows the general appointment term.
Participant exit or a broken link triggers the specified restart.
The completed electronic record must be tamper-evident.

course-validity.summary: Preserve valid official Nevada completion evidence and keep unrelated identity-assessment metrics separate.

sections.heading: Validity and documentation
sections.body: NAC 240.270 makes the required successful-completion certificate valid ninety days after issuance and specifies the SOS validation stamp. The official LMS separately states that training, examinations and payment must be completed within ninety days for validity. Save the completion notification or certificate in the stated screenshot or PDF form and attach it through SilverFlume with the supporting packet and payment.

sections.heading: Verified assessment scope
sections.body: The original materials reviewed establish the instructional minimum and the existence of the Commission Exam, but do not establish its numerical question count, duration or passing threshold. NAC 240.697 does state five-question, eighty-percent, two-minute criteria for a remote principal's dynamic KBA identity assessment. Those are identity rules for a signer, so they supply no Commission Exam threshold. An independent study score also cannot establish official completion.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A learner finds an eighty-percent number in the remote identity regulation and considers treating it as the Commission Exam passing score. The learner keeps that specification with principal identity proofing and instead relies on the actual official exam completion notification for application evidence. The ordinary numeric threshold remains unverified in this content.

keyFacts: The course certificate has ninety-day validity.
The LMS includes payment in its ninety-day instruction.
Preserve official completion evidence.
Remote principal KBA metrics do not establish Commission Exam specifications.

truthful-certificate.summary: Certify the act actually performed and apply Nevada's document-completeness and refusal boundaries.

sections.heading: Prohibited certification
sections.body: NRS 240.075 prohibits knowingly false certification, deceptive acts including journal alteration, stamps without certificates, signature-only documents and the listed vital-record/divorce-decree photocopy certifications. The ordinary copy power does not waive those exclusions. NAC 240.310 permits the signer to fill information spaces, mark them not applicable or line them through, with a limited rule for clearly excluded additional-signer lines.

sections.heading: Judgment and record protection
sections.body: The statute permits refusal when the officer is unsatisfied about capacity, competence or knowing and voluntary signing, and preserves other refusal authority subject to law. NRS 240.145 restricts completed certificates used in promotional mailings. NRS 240.147 prohibits knowing destruction, defacement or concealment of notarial records. A clean stamp impression, a customer waiver or a generous payment does not establish the truth of a false certificate.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A form's information fields are complete and a separate additional-signer line remains blank. The officer evaluates whether the current notarization clearly excludes that line under NAC 240.310. If it does, the line has a different treatment from unresolved transaction information. The officer still performs and documents the requested lawful act accurately.

keyFacts: No stamp is affixed without a notarial certificate.
Knowingly false certification is prohibited.
Unused information spaces follow the completion rule.
Competence and voluntary-execution concerns can support refusal.

articles.keyword: nevada ordinary travel quotes and journal evidence
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Ordinary Travel Quotes and Journal Evidence
articles.description: Apply Nevada's request, disclosure, rate-band and journal requirements to a mobile ordinary appointment.
articles.h1: Nevada Ordinary Travel Quotes and Journal Evidence
articles.lede: A travel charge has its own prerequisites and evidence. A lawful acknowledgment fee does not answer every question about the trip.

sections.heading: Obtain a real travel request
sections.body: A customer asks a Carson City notary to visit a care facility. NRS 240.100(3) permits an additional ordinary travel charge when the requester asks for travel, receives the explanation that the amount is additional and not required by law, and agrees in advance on the hourly rate. Arriving first and announcing an unexpected charge afterward does not follow that sequence.

sections.heading: Apply the applicable hourly band
sections.body: The statute caps requested travel between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m. at fifteen dollars per hour and between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m. at thirty dollars per hour. It permits a two-hour minimum and requires pro rata charging after the first two hours. Keep the travel quote distinct from the fee for each actual notarial service so that one amount does not conceal an excessive component.

sections.heading: Address a canceled trip
sections.body: Subsection (4) addresses a requester who cancels after the notary begins traveling, or an act that cannot be performed because of the actions of the requester or another necessary participant. It preserves the compliant agreed additional travel amount in those circumstances. The provision should be applied to the trip and actual facts. It does not create permission to invent unrelated penalties or describe an unperformed act as completed.

sections.heading: Make the required evidence
sections.body: For each additional travel fee charged, subsection (5) requires the fee amount and the dates and times travel began and ended in the journal. The ordinary act entry also has its own fields under NRS 240.120. An office can therefore reconstruct both the notarial service and the travel basis from actual recorded details. A single total receipt does not supply every statutory journal item.

faqs.q: Can the officer choose any hourly rate by agreement?
faqs.a: The advance agreement remains subject to the statutory time-band ceilings.

faqs.q: Does cancellation after departure always erase the agreed travel fee?
faqs.a: Subsection (4) preserves the compliant agreed amount in the stated cancellation circumstance.

articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Coworker Journal Signature Exceptions
articles.description: Evaluate every condition of Nevada's limited journal-signature exception without omitting the rest of the entry.
articles.lede: A familiar coworker can still require a complete ordinary journal entry. Nevada's exception concerns one field under cumulative conditions.

sections.heading: Identify the actual request
sections.body: An office notary frequently handles a colleague's routine business records. The colleague asks to skip signing the journal to save time. NRS 240.120(3) requires a prior act for that person within the previous six months, personal knowledge of identity, and the specified employer or coworker relationship with an ordinary-course business transaction. Friendship alone does not establish that whole combination.

sections.heading: Keep the exception limited
sections.body: When all the conditions apply, the notary need not require the person's journal signature. The exception does not eliminate the entry or its other required details. The date, document title, fees if any, oath indication and certificate type still identify the service. Subsection (4) specifies known personally as the identity-evidence description when the signature exception is used.

sections.heading: Do not confuse grouping with omission
sections.body: Subsection (2) separately allows one entry for more than one act when the same person and time and one-document or similar-document conditions apply. That grouping option has a different purpose from the signature exception. An office should identify which provision supports each decision. Combining several unrelated clients into one daily total does not follow the same-person and same-time conditions.

sections.heading: Preserve a usable journal
sections.body: The ordinary journal is bound with preprinted page numbers and kept securely between entries. It is open to public inspection, and the officer supplies the specified certified entry copy on request and fee payment. A careful entry should therefore explain the actual work even when a permitted signature omission or grouping option is used. Familiarity does not make transaction evidence unnecessary.

faqs.q: Can any personally known returning customer omit the signature?
faqs.a: The statutory exception also requires the recent prior act and specified business relationship conditions.

faqs.q: Does a combined entry eliminate the journal's other fields?
faqs.a: The option permits documenting multiple qualifying acts together while preserving the required transaction information.

articles.keyword: broken nevada remote sessions and retained evidence
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Broken Nevada Remote Sessions and Retained Evidence
articles.description: Restart remote performance and preserve recordings when Nevada's session requirements are interrupted.
articles.h1: Broken Nevada Remote Sessions and Retained Evidence
articles.lede: A brief reconnection can create a legal restart obligation. The recording's retention also survives failure to complete the act.

sections.heading: Recognize the restart event
sections.body: During a Nevada remote appointment, the principal exits to find another attachment. NAC 240.680 requires starting performance from the beginning when the principal or officer exits, when the audiovisual link breaks, or when the specified quality compromise prevents completion. The restart includes confirming identity again. An unchanged username or open document tab does not remove that stated requirement.

sections.heading: Reestablish the subject document
sections.body: After reconnecting, the officer applies the required identity process and identifies the electronic document as the one on which the principal executed the signature under NAC 240.678. Two similarly named files can contain different terms or attachments. The officer should establish the actual record involved in the restarted act before making a certificate that describes a completed service.

sections.heading: Keep participants informed
sections.body: NRS 240.1995 requires the officer to inform all participants before the audiovisual act that it will be electronically recorded. Personal-knowledge and credible-witness routes also have specified recorded explanations. The session evidence should reflect the method actually used. A customer who is paying does not become the only person entitled to the advance recording notice.

sections.heading: Retain unsuccessful-session evidence
sections.body: The same statute requires recordings to be kept for at least seven years regardless of whether the act was completed. NAC 240.682 protects recordings and disclosed identifying information from unauthorized access. NAC 240.710 keeps the recording outside the electronic journal itself. A canceled appointment therefore calls for protected record handling alongside an accurate description of what occurred.

faqs.q: Can the officer resume only at the stamp after a broken link?
faqs.a: The rule requires restarting performance, including identity confirmation.

faqs.q: May an incomplete act's recording be deleted immediately?
faqs.a: The statute expressly requires at least seven years of recording retention even without completion.

articles.keyword: nevada adjoining-state work and annual evidence
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Adjoining-State Work and Annual Evidence
articles.description: Track the Nevada work connection, additional affidavits and annual evidence for an adjoining-state appointee.
articles.h1: Nevada Adjoining-State Work and Annual Evidence
articles.lede: A qualifying Nevada job supports the adjoining-state route. The connection continues to matter after the initial packet is approved.

sections.heading: Establish the work connection
sections.body: A California resident works regularly at a Nevada facility operated by an employer registered to do business in the state. NRS 240.015 permits the specified adjoining-state route. The alternative concerns a Nevada place of business registered under the state business-license law and applicable local requirements. Occasional Nevada customers alone should not be assumed to establish either statutory connection.

sections.heading: Assemble the supporting packet
sections.body: NRS 240.030(2) calls for the stated residence and work-address affidavit. Self-employed applicants supply the specified state and local business licenses. An employed applicant supplies employer license copies and an employer affidavit describing regular work at the Nevada office, business or facility. The bond and oath are filed in the Nevada county of that qualifying business or employment, with the required county certification.

sections.heading: Calendar the annual evidence
sections.body: NRS 240.031 requires the adjoining-state notary to submit the stated business-license copies and subsection 240.030(2) information annually within thirty days before the appointment anniversary. This is a recurring obligation during the term. It is distinct from the four-year appointment renewal and from a private employer's internal license calendar. Identify the appointment anniversary when planning the submission.

sections.heading: Respond to a work change
sections.body: If the qualifying business or regular employment connection ceases, NRS 240.015 permits suspension and provides a conditional reinstatement route before term expiration. NRS 240.036 also addresses timely amendment of a nonresident's business or employment information. The officer should report actual changes through the stated procedures. A continuing vendor subscription does not establish the lost Nevada work qualification.

faqs.q: Does a Nevada appointment authorize acts while the officer is in California?
faqs.a: NRS 240.020 does not confer another state's acting authority.

faqs.q: Is the annual license evidence the same as four-year renewal?
faqs.a: It is a separate annual obligation tied to the appointment anniversary.

articles.keyword: lost, damaged and amended nevada stamps
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Lost, Damaged and Amended Nevada Stamps
articles.description: Distinguish Nevada's different stamp events and the required appointment evidence for replacement.
articles.h1: Lost, Damaged and Amended Nevada Stamps
articles.lede: A missing device, an inoperable device and amended appointment information have different statutory triggers. Each requires attention to the actual appointment record.

sections.heading: Classify a lost device
sections.body: NRS 240.045 requires a request for an amended appointment certificate within ten days after a stamp is lost, on the prescribed form with the ten-dollar fee. The officer obtains a replacement under the amendment procedure. A simple reorder using an old vendor receipt does not account for the required state request. The loss date therefore matters when planning the response.

sections.heading: Handle physical damage promptly
sections.body: If the stamp is destroyed, broken, damaged or otherwise inoperable, subsection (2) requires immediate SOS notification and a new stamp. This event has its own wording and timing. Continuing to apply unreadable impressions does not satisfy NRS 240.040's legibility requirement. The officer should distinguish an authentic but unusable device from a current working replacement.

sections.heading: Use the amended details
sections.body: After an amended appointment certificate, NRS 240.036(5) directs destruction of the former stamp, a replacement containing the amended information and notice to the bond surety. The stamp's name, expiration and appointment number identify the commissioned authority. Leaving obsolete information on a device while the state record changes can defeat the purpose of the amendment process.

sections.heading: Give the supplier valid evidence
sections.body: NRS 240.045(3) prevents manufacture without presentation of the original or amended appointment certificate or a certified copy. The new device must still produce the prescribed indelible reproducible and legible rectangular impression, with nonresident wording where applicable. Secure custody under NRS 240.040 and NAC 240.300 continues when the device is not in use. A coworker's stamp cannot substitute for the officer's replacement.

faqs.q: Does the ten-day lost-stamp period also describe broken-stamp notice?
faqs.a: The broken or inoperable-stamp subsection instead requires immediate notification.

faqs.q: Can a supplier rely solely on a business card?
faqs.a: The statute requires the specified appointment-certificate evidence before manufacture.

articles.keyword: nevada directed signatures for physical inability
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Directed Signatures for Physical Inability
articles.description: Apply Nevada's other-person signing accommodation while preserving appearance and accurate certificate wording.
articles.h1: Nevada Directed Signatures for Physical Inability
articles.lede: Physical inability to write can be accommodated under Nevada's specific procedure. The notarial officer remains distinct from the person directed to sign.

sections.heading: Identify the trigger and direction
sections.body: A care-facility resident understands the transaction but cannot physically sign the presented document. NRS 240.1655(8) permits that person to direct another person to sign the resident's name. The provision addresses physical inability and a directed execution. A family member's desire to finish quickly does not alone supply the principal's direction or establish the statutory trigger.

sections.heading: Keep the officer out of the helper role
sections.body: The statute expressly requires someone other than the notarial officer to act as the directed signer. An officer familiar with a different state's procedure should check this Nevada text before offering to write the principal's name personally. The helper physically executes the directed signature, while the notary evaluates and certifies the lawful act using the required identity and certificate procedures.

sections.heading: Bring both participants before the officer
sections.body: NAC 240.340 requires both the physically unable person and directed helper to appear before the notary when the document is signed. Sending the helper later with a completed page does not follow that stated appearance condition. The regulation also supplies a sufficient acknowledgment form for the described situation. Accurate completion should describe who appeared and the directed execution that actually occurred.

sections.heading: Add the explanatory notation
sections.body: Section 240.1655(8) requires wording identifying the helper who affixed the signature and the person who directed it, or similar wording. The explanation provides context for a name written by another person. The officer still evaluates prohibited family or interest relationships and the truth of the certificate. This accommodation does not waive an independent statutory disqualification.

faqs.q: May the Nevada notary be the directed helper?
faqs.a: This provision requires a person other than the notarial officer.

faqs.q: Can only the helper attend after signing at home?
faqs.a: The regulation requires both principal and helper before the officer when signing occurs.

articles.keyword: nevada blank information and additional signer lines
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Blank Information and Additional Signer Lines
articles.description: Apply Nevada's completeness rule and its limited treatment of an additional signature line outside the current act.
articles.h1: Nevada Blank Information and Additional Signer Lines
articles.lede: An unused information space and an absent additional signature do not always have the same treatment. Nevada's regulation describes the distinction.

sections.heading: Resolve the information fields
sections.body: NRS 240.075 prohibits the described notarial act on an incomplete document requiring signer information. NAC 240.310 provides ways the signer can satisfy completeness by supplying information, marking a space not applicable or lining it through. An officer should inspect which spaces are unresolved and ask the principal to address them through the allowed process. Inventing the customer's missing terms does not follow that rule.

sections.heading: Evaluate an additional signature line
sections.body: Subsection (2) addresses a blank line designated for an additional signer when the remainder of the document satisfies subsection (1) and it is clear the current notarization does not apply to that blank line. A seller's acknowledgment can therefore raise a different question from an entirely blank payment clause. The officer should identify the scope of the present certificate accurately.

sections.heading: Complete a real certificate
sections.body: The same chapter prohibits stamping a record without a notarial certificate and performing an act on a document containing only a signature. Removing every printed term to leave a signed blank sheet is therefore no solution. The certificate must evidence the actual act under NRS 240.1655, including the relevant name, location, official signature, date and stamped statement.

sections.heading: Keep evidence faithful
sections.body: The journal is entered when the act is performed and describes the document, identity route, oath indication and certificate type with the other required fields. If the act cannot lawfully proceed, a stamp should not be supplied merely to satisfy a recipient's demand. The distinction between an excluded additional-signer line and unresolved transaction information should be evaluated from the actual record presented.

faqs.q: Must every blank additional-signer line always be removed?
faqs.a: The rule permits the specified situation when the current notarization clearly excludes that line and the rest is complete.

faqs.q: Does a certificate permit knowingly false document certification?
faqs.a: NRS 240.075 independently prohibits certifying an instrument containing a statement the officer knows is false.

articles.keyword: overseas principals and nevada remote location
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Overseas Principals and Nevada Remote Location
articles.description: Evaluate the principal's confirmed United States connection and the officer's actual Nevada location.
articles.h1: Overseas Principals and Nevada Remote Location
articles.lede: Remote service can involve several places at once. Nevada assigns different significance to the officer's location, the principal's location and the document's connection.

sections.heading: Locate the officer physically
sections.body: A Nevada electronic notary is asked to assist an overseas signer while the officer is traveling. NRS 240.1993(2) requires the officer to be physically in Nevada at the time, regardless of the principal's location. A Nevada home office, mailing address or server does not establish where the traveling person is actually sitting during the proposed session.

sections.heading: Check the foreign prohibition condition
sections.body: For a principal outside the United States, subsection (1)(c) requires that the notary have no actual knowledge of prohibition in the jurisdiction where the person is physically located. That condition operates with the required document connection. A client's willingness to proceed does not make actual knowledge disappear. Record the true participant locations when evaluating whether the proposed route fits.

sections.heading: Obtain the principal's connection confirmation
sections.body: The person electronically signing must confirm that the act and document concern the specified United States court, government or other entity matter, United States property, or a substantially United States-connected transaction. A Nevada property agreement provides a concrete property connection to examine. A domestic cloud account alone does not establish those substantive categories.

sections.heading: Perform the complete session
sections.body: The normal identity, audiovisual, recording, electronic certificate and journal duties continue. NRS 240.1991 requires simultaneous interaction and real-time transmission, while NRS 240.1995 governs recording and recorded identity explanations. A permitted location combination is one component of lawful service. It does not substitute for the full identity process, a correct subject document or tamper-evident completion.

faqs.q: Can the officer complete the act from another state using a Nevada account?
faqs.a: The statute requires the officer's physical presence in Nevada.

faqs.q: Is any document on a United States server sufficiently connected?
faqs.a: The statute identifies substantive matter, property or transaction connections confirmed by the principal.

articles.keyword: nevada employer property, fees and official credentials
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Employer Property, Fees and Official Credentials
articles.description: Apply Nevada's ownership, fee-scope and personal credential controls when workplace demands affect notarial service.
articles.h1: Nevada Employer Property, Fees and Official Credentials
articles.lede: A workplace can fund the appointment and organize appointments. Nevada still assigns specific property and official duties to the commissioned person.

sections.heading: Separate funding from ownership
sections.body: An employer purchases the stamp and journal and later claims the items when the notary leaves. NRS 240.143 expressly treats the stamp, journal and appointment certificate as the notary's personal property. Withholding them is unlawful regardless of who provided the purchase money. The employer's accounting treatment does not amend this statutory allocation of the items.

sections.heading: Check the scope of fee control
sections.body: NRS 240.100(6) permits an employer to prohibit fees for acts performed within employment scope. It also forbids requiring surrender of all or part of fees earned outside that scope. A weekend private appointment and an assigned office appointment can therefore raise different scope questions. Identify the actual work rather than assuming the original supply purchase transfers every future service fee.

sections.heading: Preserve the actual officer's control
sections.body: NRS 240.075 bars another person's use of the stamp or signing the notary's name in a notarial capacity. The electronic signature and seal likewise remain protected under NRS 240.202. A trained assistant can help arrange an appointment, but the staff relationship does not authorize use of the officer's official credentials to complete acts while the officer is absent.

sections.heading: Recognize employer consequences
sections.body: NRS 240.150 addresses employer exposure when the notary's misconduct occurs within employment scope and the employer consents. The employer also has duties under the non-English advertising provision. A workplace instruction is therefore no reason to suppress a required notice or use a misleading professional title. The commissioned officer and employer should each follow their applicable legal responsibilities.

faqs.q: May the employer retain the journal because it bought the book?
faqs.a: The statutory personal-property and no-withholding rule applies regardless of funding.

faqs.q: May the employer demand fees from outside-scope work?
faqs.a: Section 240.100(6) forbids compelling surrender of those outside-scope fees.

articles.keyword: nevada remote identity privacy and separate records
articles.intent: Resolve a specific Nevada notarial work scenario
articles.title: Nevada Remote Identity Privacy and Separate Records
articles.description: Keep principal KBA metrics, protected identity information, journal entries and recordings in their correct Nevada roles.
articles.h1: Nevada Remote Identity Privacy and Separate Records
articles.lede: A remote identity check can produce sensitive evidence. Nevada's rules prescribe both the process and the handling of the resulting records.

sections.heading: Use the whole identity route
sections.body: The documentary remote route combines a government credential with photo and signature, credential analysis and the required dynamic KBA or authorized proofing process. NAC 240.670 prevents further completion using a credential when validity or the person's feature match cannot be established. A clear-looking credential alone does not automatically supply every component of that route.

sections.heading: Keep KBA metrics attached to identity
sections.body: NAC 240.697 requires five principal questions with at least five possible answers each, eighty percent correct within two minutes and the specified limited retries with replacement questions. It also requires confidentiality of the questions and answers. These metrics govern principal identity assessment. They do not establish a passing percentage, question count or duration for the notary's Commission Exam.

sections.heading: Limit the electronic journal
sections.body: NAC 240.710 excludes personally identifying information unless legally required in the journal, and excludes the remote recording itself. The journal still contains its statutory transaction fields and notes remote use under NRS 240.201. A platform should therefore preserve separate protected evidence stores. Adding every possible identifier to a public-facing entry is not a substitute for the prescribed content limits.

sections.heading: Protect access and backups
sections.body: NAC 240.682 requires the officer and provider to protect recordings and disclosed identifying information against unauthorized access. NAC 240.708 requires secure journal backup and prevents post-entry deletion or alteration of content or sequence. Recording disclosure follows NAC 240.686's authorized categories. An ordinary journal inspection request does not automatically authorize release of all audiovisual and identity materials.

faqs.q: Is the eighty-percent KBA rule the Commission Exam passing score?
faqs.a: It is a principal identity-assessment specification and does not establish that exam threshold.

faqs.q: Should the remote recording be embedded in the electronic journal?
faqs.a: NAC 240.710 expressly excludes the required recording from that journal.
